concerns.text: The validation design is circular/tautological. The spec proposes to validate a 'modality gap' by comparing a proxy model's performance on 'symbolic tokens' (derived via FR-002) against its performance on 'physical control (mapped)' (derived via the same FR-002 logic). If the 'logical rules' in FR-002 deterministically map continuous vectors to discrete labels, then the 'physical control' baseline is mathematically identical to the 'symbolic' target. Comparing a model's ability to predict a label against its ability to predict the *same* label (just via a different input modality) does not measure a 'modality gap' in representational capacity; it measures the model's ability to learn the mapping function itself. The 'gap' is an artifact of the transformation, not a property of the world model. The validation target (performance on mapped physical data) is definitionally dependent on the predictor construction (the mapping rules).

The claimed relationship (performance degradation) is not empirically testable as stated because the 'physical control' baseline is not an independent ground truth. The spec assumes the 'physical control' task is 'mapped to discrete success/failure' (US-2). If this mapping uses the same logical rules as the symbolic task, the two tasks are identical in label space. If they use different rules, the comparison is confounded by rule complexity, not modality. A valid test requires an *independent* ground truth for physical success (e.g., a physics engine simulator score) that is NOT derived from the same logical rules used to create the symbolic tokens. Currently, the spec validates the metric against a quantity (mapped physical success) that is trivially determined by the metric's own input construction.

The statistical method (paired t-test) is inappropriate for the proposed data structure. The spec compares 'symbolic' vs 'physical-mapped' performance. If the 'physical-mapped' labels are derived from the same continuous vectors as the 'symbolic' labels (via FR-002), the samples are not independent, and the 'paired' nature of the test assumes a specific dependency structure that may not exist if the mapping introduces noise. More critically, if the labels are identical (as suspected in the circularity issue), the t-test will simply test for noise in the model's prediction of the *same* label, which is a trivial finding, not a scientific one.
